acceptanceCriteria: The SDD contract names the acceptance mode for requirements written under a standing approval, REQUIREMENTS.tsv (or the spec header) carries it, and one audit command lists requirements never read back by the owner.
body:
Open question, not a defect. docs/SPEC-DRIVEN-DEVELOPMENT.md defines `accepted` as 'explicitly approved by the repository owner' and product invariant 8 says generated or inferred documentation can propose intent but cannot accept it. Since the owner's standing auto-accept of lane requirements on 2026-10-11, every requirement a lane writes becomes `accepted` in the same PR that implements it (CEM-V1-140..232, DCW-V0-048..056, this week alone), so the status no longer separates owner-reviewed intent from agent-authored intent, and the authority ladder's top rung is filled by the lane that is also filling rungs 3 and 4.

Expected: either (a) a distinct intent status (`accepted-standing` or `auto-accepted`) that names the standing-approval record and the date, promotable to `accepted` only by an owner read-back, with REQUIREMENTS.tsv carrying the mode so an audit can list every requirement the owner never read; or (b) a periodic owner acceptance batch (the build-log already has 'Owner acceptances' entries) that converts auto-accepted rows, with a gate that refuses `validated` delivery status on an auto-accepted requirement.
Actual: `accepted` is written by the lane; no row distinguishes the two.

Version: origin/main 88197e465 (2026-10-13). Source: SDD review by the orchestrating session for decisions 0523/0525 after PRs #850..#855.
title: governance: the standing auto-accept of lane requirements (since 2026-10-11) makes `accepted` intent status undiscriminating; record the acceptance mode in the status
